sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from an unknown discrete-confounder law with fixed known overlap constant \(\epsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: Null cells are permitted; positivity is imposed only when \(p_k>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell masses, propensities, and arm means are unknown. Estimators may use the known inputs \(n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma\), must guard every denominator, and must return a value for every sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2--4 establish binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity rates, while Section 4.2 leaves intermediate maximal-radius dependence open.
The accepted same-class parent proves lower rate \(b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\) and upper rate \(n^{-1}+\min\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\).
A chi-square functional modulus is dual to a bias--variance optimization under convexity and compactness conditions.
Heavy--light polynomial estimation matches moment-based converses for separable large-alphabet functionals.

tldr: The kernel is the finite-sample minimax MSE frontier for an identified ATE when high-dimensional discrete adjustment cells have effects within a calibrated maximal radius \(\sigma M\) of the ATE.  The exact split-sample empirical-mass estimator gives collision-scale risk \(M^2/n\) for \(2\le d\le n\) when \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\), while the inherited rare-cell approximation branch gives the same rate when \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), equivalently \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\).  Thus approximate common effects retain collision-scale estimation on the union of these two directly checkable regions.  At the still-unresolved benchmark \(d=n\), \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), an exactly normalized shared-design marked family fails because its global outcome shift makes the full mixtures distinguishable; the conditionally centered marked-coupling repair remains open, and no global frontier formula is asserted.

project_justification.gap: The closest published work gives the binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity endpoints and explicitly leaves maximal-radius dependence unresolved.  The accepted same-class parent gives a nonmatching bracket; the present results close the additional union \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\) for \(d\le n\), but not the remaining radius-dependent wedge.
project_justification.niche: Unknown random cell masses, unknown overlapping propensities, empty cells, supportwise centering around the ATE, and only conditional second moments make the residual converse neither fixed-design shrinkage nor a routine polynomial-functional problem.  The corrected residual wedge additionally enforces \(u_{n,d}>n^{-1}\), so already-closed approximation-scale points are excluded.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a total empirical-mass estimator, proves collision-scale minimax risk on the union of the empirical and rare-cell approximation regions, and rules out the displayed global-shift prior family.  For lower-bound transfer, the published binary anchor embeds in the present real-outcome class through \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\), which scales ATEs and squared risks by \(M\) and \(M^2\).  For the real-outcome upper bound, the declared envelopes imply \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\).  A conditionally centered shared-design converse remains an explicit open question.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, revised 2026) provide the binary-outcome baseline in Theorems 2--4; Section 4.2 identifies the unresolved radius dependence and discusses extension under bounded conditional second moments.  Their binary anchor transfers into the present centered real-outcome class by \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\): conditional means then lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\), conditional central variances are at most \(M^2/4\), ATE separations scale by \(M\), and squared-error lower bounds scale by \(M^2\).  Conversely, the real-outcome upper analysis uses only \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\), not bounded outcomes.  Section 7's 401(k) eligibility and net-assets analysis is the consumer but does not validate overlap or its reported intervals.  The internal accepted parent supplies the same-class bracket and the channel and factorial-lift results.  Zeng et al.'s cited polynomial-functional literature informs the approximation and mixture architectures; the remaining law-by-law shared-design construction is stated separately as an open question.
technical_internal_limitation: A hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer gives only product-scale separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering at \(\sigma=0\).  The explicit family \(\Pi_h^\star\) further shows that exact normalization, identical design marginals, supportwise radius, and separated ATEs are not sufficient: its hypothesis-wide outcome shift yields a sign test with total variation tending to one at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\).  The newly closed approximation branch removes every \(d\le n\) point with \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\) from the residual problem.  Any replacement converse must operate in the corrected wedge, eliminate the globally visible first-order coefficient, and control the full marked likelihood.
honest_scope: Consistency and exchangeability identify the displayed ATE.  The established claims are the empirical-mass risk bound, the refined infimum-risk bracket, collision-scale minimax risk for \(2\le d\le n\) whenever \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), and failure of the displayed global-shift prior.  The open domain \(\mathcal W\) requires \(n^{-1}<u_{n,d}<1\) in addition to \(d>n\) or \(\sigma^2d^2>n\); the marked-prior repair remains open inside that domain.  No global sharp rate, unspecified selector, unknown-radius adaptation, confidence interval, bounded-outcome assumption, overlap validation, or claim about the reported 401(k) intervals is included.

symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed known lower bound on both treatment probabilities in occupied cells.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Fixed known scale for conditional means, conditional central variances, and effect heterogeneity.

symbols.name: \(\sigma\)
symbols.def: Fixed known maximal conditional-effect radius in units of \(M\).

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P))^2]\), where the infimum ranges over all observed-sample estimators.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}:=J_k^{(0)}(\overline Y_{1k}^{(0)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(0)})\); hence it is zero in an empty or one-arm-only pilot cell.

symbols.name: \(R_0\)
symbols.def: \(R_0:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}\), the total pilot occupancy in cells containing both arms.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal W\)
symbols.def: The unresolved parameter set defined in \(\mathrm{def:residual\text{-}wedge}\).

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Index of the two benchmark mixture hypotheses.

symbols.name: \(\Pi_h^\star\)
symbols.space: probability measures on one-unit full-data laws
symbols.def: Uniform pushforward of \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) through \(z\mapsto P_{h,z}^\star\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb Q_h^\star\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\rho_n\)
symbols.def: Maximal normalized ATE separation derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:repair\text{-}benchmark\text{-}prior}\) under its support and mixture-distance constraints.

standard.name: fixed positivity on occupied discrete cells

assumptions.condition: \(-M/2\le\mu_{ak}\le M/2\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

standard.name: bounded conditional-mean envelope, centered real-outcome variant

assumptions.condition: \(v_{ak}\le M^2\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

novel.justification: A calibrated \(\sigma\) is a substantive bound on effect modification across prespecified adjustment cells. It is satisfied by approximately common-effect scientific models and can be varied as a transparent sensitivity parameter rather than selected to optimize an estimator.

definitions.name: Radius-constrained discrete-confounder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\{P:\text{ for the displayed }n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma,\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}envelope},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}moment\text{-}envelope},\mathrm{ass:maximal\text{-}effect\text{-}radius}\}\).

definitions.name: Total clipped occupancy-weighted pilot
definitions.construction: On records \(1,\ldots,m_0\), form \(N_{ak}^{(0)}\), \(N_k^{(0)}\), \(J_k^{(0)}\), the guarded means \(\overline Y_{ak}^{(0)}\), and \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}\). Set \(R_0=\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}\), use \(w_k^{(0)}=N_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}/R_0\) when \(R_0>0\) and \(w_k^{(0)}=0\) when \(R_0=0\), and return \(\widetilde\tau=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}(\sum_{k=1}^dw_k^{(0)}\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)})\). Thus an empty pilot, an entirely unmatched pilot, and every empty or one-arm-only pilot cell contribute zero, and every denominator is guarded.

definitions.name: Empirical-mass correction of the exact occupancy pilot
definitions.construction: For \(n\ge8\), compute exactly the \(\widetilde\tau\) in \(\mathrm{def:occupancy\text{-}pilot}\) on the first \(m_0\) records. On the remaining \(m_1\) records form the guarded correction-block quantities and set \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left[\widetilde\tau+\frac1{m_1}\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}J_k^{(1)}\{\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}-\widetilde\tau\}\right].\] An empty or entirely unmatched correction block returns \(\widetilde\tau\), while empty and one-arm-only correction cells contribute zero. For \(3\le n<8\), set \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}:=0\).

definitions.name: Residual wedge after the parent endpoints and both collision-scale regions
Exactly normalized shared-design global-shift marked family
definitions.construction: Fix \(d=n\), \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), \(h\in\{-1,1\}\), and \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\). Define \(P_{h,z}^\star\) by \(p_k=1/n\), \(\pi_k=1/2\), and \(\tau_k=h\Delta_n^\star+(M\sigma_n^\star/2)z_k\). Set \(\mu_{ak}=(2a-1)\tau_k/2\). Conditional on \(X=k\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); independently draw each \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\) with \(P\{Y(a)=M/2\mid X=k\}=1/2+(2a-1)\tau_k/(2M)\), and set \(Y=Y(A)\). Let \(\Pi_h^\star\) be uniform over \(\{P_{h,z}^\star:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}\). Every support law is exactly normalized, has the same deterministic design \((p_k,\pi_k)=(1/n,1/2)\), satisfies \(\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)=h\Delta_n^\star\), and obeys \(\max_k|\tau_k-\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)|\le M\sigma_n^\star/2\).

definitions.name: Conditionally centered marked-coupling handle
definitions.construction: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), replace the common shift in \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}marked\text{-}family}\) by a bounded mark score centered conditionally on the shared design, couple that score differently to the arm means under \(h=-1\) and \(h=1\), impose exact mass normalization before mixing, and optimize \(\rho_n\) subject to supportwise radius and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\).

statements.statement: Let \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}\) be exactly the estimator in \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}estimator}\), whose pilot is exactly \(\mathrm{def:occupancy\text{-}pilot}\). There is \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(n\ge3\), \(2\le d\le n\), \(0\le\sigma\le2\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), \[E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2\frac{d^2}{n^2}\right).\]
statements.justification: The exact total estimator resolves a polynomial benchmark gap and supplies a stable low-degree branch under conditional second moments.
statements.gap: Zeng et al.'s binary-outcome occupancy analysis yields a term of order \(\sigma^2+d/n^2+1/n\); this real-outcome empirical-mass correction multiplies \(\sigma^2\) by squared unmatched mass for \(d\le n\).
statements.consumer: For \(d=\lfloor n^{3/4}\rfloor\) and \(\sigma^2=u_{n,d}\), it certifies MSE of order \(M^2/n\) for sparse categorical adjustment.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m=m_1\), \(t=\widetilde\tau\), \(e=t-\tau(P)\), and
\[
 \delta_k=\tau_k-\tau(P),\qquad
 U=\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}(1-J_k^{(1)}),\qquad
 S=\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}\delta_k.
\]
All three quantities are defined even when cells or blocks are empty by \(\mathrm{def:occupancy\text{-}pilot}\) and \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}estimator}\).  The mean envelope gives \(|\tau_k|\leq M\) on occupied cells and hence \(|\tau(P)|\leq M\).  The maximal-radius assumption gives \(|\delta_k|\leq\sigma M\), while the definition of \(\tau(P)\) gives
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^dp_k\delta_k
 =\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\tau_k-\tau(P)\sum_{k=1}^dp_k=0.
\]

We first prove the needed unmatched-mass estimate.  Put
\[
 s_{ak}=P(X=k,A=a),\qquad
 V_{ak}=N_{ak}^{(1)}\mathbf 1\{N_{1-a,k}^{(1)}=0\}.
\]
Then \(mU=\sum_{k,a}V_{ak}\) exactly: an unmatched nonempty cell contributes its entire occupancy in its unique observed arm, and an empty or matched cell contributes zero.  Fix \((a,k)\), set \(\alpha=s_{ak}\) and \(\beta=s_{1-a,k}\), and use the multinomial factorial-moment identities supplied by iid sampling.  Since \(N^2=N(N-1)+N\),
\[
 E[V_{ak}^2]
 =m\alpha(1-\beta)^{m-1}
  +m(m-1)\alpha^2(1-\beta)^{m-2}.
\]
For distinct cells \(k\ne\ell\), if \(\gamma=s_{c\ell}\) and \(\phi=s_{1-c,\ell}\), the same identity gives
\[
 E[V_{ak}V_{c\ell}]
 =m(m-1)\alpha\gamma(1-\beta-\phi)^{m-2},
\]
whereas \(V_{0k}V_{1k}=0\).  Overlap implies
\(
 \alpha\leq\epsilon^{-1}\beta
\)
and
\(
 \gamma\leq\epsilon^{-1}\phi
\);
these inequalities also hold when the relevant cell mass is zero.  For \(m\geq4\), \((1-x)^r\leq e^{-rx}\) and the finite bounds on \(\sup_{x\geq0}xe^{-x}\) and \(\sup_{x\geq0}x^2e^{-x}\) therefore yield
\[
 E[V_{ak}^2]\leq C_{\epsilon},
 \qquad
 E[V_{ak}V_{c\ell}]\leq C_{\epsilon}\quad(k\ne\ell).
\]
There are \(2d\) diagonal terms and fewer than \(4d^2\) ordered cross terms.  Consequently,
\[
 E[U^2]\leq C_{\epsilon}\frac{d^2}{m^2}.
\]
The deterministic inequality \(0\leq U\leq1\) supplies the uniform refinement
\[
 E[U^2]\leq C_{\epsilon}\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{m^2}\right\}. \tag{1}
\]

Next isolate the correction-block outcome noise
\[
 W=\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}J_k^{(1)}
 \left\{(\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\mu_{1k})
 -(\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}-\mu_{0k})\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathscr G\) be generated by the pilot and all correction-block \((X,A)\) values.  Iid sampling makes the outcome residuals conditionally independent across observations, and their conditional means vanish.  Thus \(E[W\mid\mathscr G]=0\), and the second-moment envelope gives
\[
 E[W^2\mid\mathscr G]
 \leq \frac{M^2}{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^d
 (N_k^{(1)})^2J_k^{(1)}
 \left(\frac1{N_{1k}^{(1)}}+\frac1{N_{0k}^{(1)}}\right). \tag{2}
\]
The displayed reciprocals occur only when \(J_k^{(1)}=1\), so no division by zero is present.  Conditional on \(N_k^{(1)}=r\), the treated count is \(B\sim\operatorname{Bin}(r,\pi_k)\).  For \(B\sim\operatorname{Bin}(r,q)\) with \(q>0\),
\[
 E\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{B>0\}}B\right]
 \leq2E\left[\frac1{B+1}\right]
 =\frac{2\{1-(1-q)^{r+1}\}}{(r+1)q}
 \leq\frac2{(r+1)q}. \tag{3}
\]
Apply (3) to the two arms, discard the other-arm indicator, and use \(\pi_k,1-\pi_k\geq\epsilon\).  The conditional expectation of the \(k\)-th summand in (2) is at most
\[
 \frac{4r^2}{(r+1)\epsilon}\leq\frac{4r}{\epsilon}.
\]
Since \(\sum_kE[N_k^{(1)}]=m\), (2) yields
\[
 E[W^2]\leq\frac{4M^2}{\epsilon m}. \tag{4}
\]

On a matched correction cell write
\(
 \widehat\Delta_k^{(1)}=\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}
\), and put
\[
 T_{\rm raw}=t+\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}J_k^{(1)}
 (\widehat\Delta_k^{(1)}-t).
\]
The value assigned to \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(1)}\) off the event \(J_k^{(1)}=1\) is immaterial because its coefficient is zero.  Before the final clipping, direct algebra in the estimator definition gives the exact identity
\[
 T_{\rm raw}-\tau(P)
 =W+S+\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}(1-J_k^{(1)})(e-\delta_k). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, expand \(T_{\rm raw}=t+m^{-1}\sum_kN_k^{(1)}J_k^{(1)}(\widehat\Delta_k^{(1)}-t)\), insert \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(1)}=\tau_k\) plus the residual defining \(W\) on matched cells, and use \(\sum_kN_k^{(1)}=m\).  Because \(m^{-1}\sum_{i=m_0+1}^n\delta_{X_i}=S\), iid sampling and the centering identity above imply
\[
 E[S]=0,\qquad E[S^2]\leq\frac{\sigma^2M^2}{m}. \tag{6}
\]
Moreover, if the last term of (5) is denoted by \(H\), then
\[
 |H|\leq U(|e|+\sigma M). \tag{7}
\]
The pilot and correction blocks are independent by iid sampling.  Hence (1) and (7) imply
\[
 E[H^2]
 \leq2\{E[e^2]+\sigma^2M^2\}E[U^2]. \tag{8}
\]
The cited matched-cell occupancy bound \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}occupancy\text{-}risk}\), applied to the first \(m_0\) records, gives
\[
 E[e^2]\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2
 \left(\sigma^2+\frac1{m_0}+\frac d{m_0^2}\right).
\]
For \(n\geq8\), \(m_0,m_1\geq n/2-1\); since \(d\leq n\), this reduces to
\[
 E[e^2]\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2(\sigma^2+n^{-1}),
 \qquad
 E[U^2]\leq C_{\epsilon}d^2/n^2. \tag{9}
\]
The conditional mean-zero property of \(W\) makes its cross term with the other terms in (5) vanish.  Applying \((x+y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\) to \(S+H\), and then using (4), (6), (8), and (9), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E[(T_{\rm raw}-\tau(P))^2]
 &\leq E[W^2]+2E[S^2]+2E[H^2]\\
 &\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac{\sigma^2}{n}
 +(\sigma^2+n^{-1})\frac{d^2}{n^2}\right\}\\
 &\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2\frac{d^2}{n^2}\right),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last line uses \(d\leq n\) and \(0\leq\sigma\leq2\).  Since \(\tau(P)\in[-M,M]\), projection onto \([-M,M]\) cannot increase squared error, so the same bound holds for \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}\).  Finally, when \(3\leq n<8\), the definition returns zero and the mean envelope gives \((0-\tau(P))^2\leq M^2\leq8M^2/n\).  Enlarging \(C_{\epsilon}\) proves the claim uniformly over every stated sample size, including null cells and entirely unmatched blocks.

statements.statement: There are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that throughout the declared parameter range, \[c_{\epsilon}M^2\{b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min(1,u_{n,d})\}\le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon}M^2q_{n,d,\sigma}^{\mathrm{em}}.\] This is an infimum-risk upper bound: for \(d\le n\) it combines \(\mathrm{lem:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}upper}\) with the inherited bounds, and for \(d>n\) it equals the accepted parent's upper envelope. No claim about an algebraically unspecified selector is part of the theorem. Relative to the accepted parent's upper rate \(n^{-1}+\min\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\), it is a strict tightening whenever \(d\le n\) and \(d/n^2+\sigma^2d^2/n^2<\min\{u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\).
statements.justification: This is the strongest justified finite-sample advance without importing unspecified estimator bytes.
statements.gap: The accepted same-class parent has the displayed lower benchmark but the larger upper radius branch \(\sigma^2+d/n^2\); the empirical-mass branch strictly improves it on the displayed nondegenerate region.
statements.consumer: It gives analysts a conservative finite-sample risk certificate before the residual wedge is solved.
statements.proof_tex:
The accepted same-class result \(\mathrm{lem:accepted\text{-}parent\text{-}bracket}\) gives, on exactly \(\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\{b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min(1,u_{n,d})\}
 \leq\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\]
and supplies a particular total data-driven estimator with risk at most
\[
 C_{\epsilon}M^2\left[\frac1n+
 \min\left\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right\}\right]. \tag{10}
\]
This proves the asserted lower inequality without changing the model class.

For the upper inequality, denote the total estimator supplied with (10) by \(T^{\rm par}\).  If \(d>n\), then \(v_{n,d}=1\), and the right side of (10) is exactly
\[
 C_{\epsilon}M^2\left[\frac1n+
 \min\left\{1,u_{n,d},\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2v_{n,d}\right\}\right]
 =C_{\epsilon}M^2q_{n,d,\sigma}^{\mathrm{em}}. \tag{11}
\]
If \(d\leq n\), then \(v_{n,d}=d^2/n^2\), and \(\mathrm{lem:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}upper}\) gives the second, total, data-driven candidate
\[
 E[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2v_{n,d}\right). \tag{12}
\]
Define one estimator from the sample by using \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}\) when \(d\leq n\) and
\[
 \sigma^2v_{n,d}
 \leq\min\left\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
\]
and using \(T^{\rm par}\) otherwise.  This rule depends only on the known inputs \((n,d,\sigma)\); both branches are total on every sample.  Combining (10) and (12), and enlarging the comparison constant to the larger branch constant, gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 &\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left[\frac1n+
 \min\left\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2},\sigma^2v_{n,d}\right\}\right]\\
 &\leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left[\frac1n+
 \min\left\{1,u_{n,d},\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2v_{n,d}\right\}\right]\\
 &=C_{\epsilon}M^2q_{n,d,\sigma}^{\mathrm{em}}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the upper inequality and exhibits the deterministic selector that witnesses it.

It remains to verify the strict-improvement clause.  When \(d\leq n\),
\(
 u_{n,d}\leq1/\log^2(en)<1
\).
If
\[
 \frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\frac{d^2}{n^2}
 <\min\left\{u_{n,d},\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
\]
then the third entry in the definition of \(q_{n,d,\sigma}^{\mathrm{em}}\) is strictly smaller than every active entry of the parent's minimum.  Adding the common term \(n^{-1}\) preserves strict inequality, proving the final assertion.

statements.statement:
Uniformly over \(2\le d\le n\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\) satisfying
\[
 \sigma^2d^2\le n
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 u_{n,d}\le \frac1n,
\]
equivalently satisfying the first inequality or \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\asymp_{\epsilon}\frac{M^2}{n}.
\]
In particular, for \(d=\lfloor n^{3/4}\rfloor\) and \(\sigma^2=u_{n,d}\), the minimax mean squared error is of order \(M^2/n\).
statements.justification: This theorem-level result combines two independently evaluable sufficient conditions: the empirical-mass branch \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) and the inherited approximation branch \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\).
statements.gap: The accepted parent leaves radius-dependent gaps, but its \(u_{n,d}\) upper branch and the empirical-mass correction together already close this full union at the collision scale.
statements.consumer: For sparse adjustment tables, the result specifies when a calibrated near-homogeneity assumption is sufficient for parametric-order ATE estimation; it does not claim necessity outside the proved union.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge3\), every support law of \(\Pi_h^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}\), the two design marginals are identical, and their ATE intervals are the singletons \(\{-\Delta_n^\star\}\) and \(\{\Delta_n^\star\}\). For the full-sample mixtures \(\mathbb Q_h^\star:=\int Q_P^{(n)}\,d\Pi_h^\star(P)\), the sign test based on \(\overline Z_n\) gives \[\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_{-1}^\star,\mathbb Q_1^\star)\ge1-2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n(\Delta_n^\star)^2}{2M^2}\right\}=1-2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{\log^2(en)}{32\log^2(e+\log^2(en))}\right\}.\] Hence this exactly normalized supportwise-radius family violates the required mixture-distance bound for all sufficiently large \(n\); the failed condition is full-mixture indistinguishability, caused by its hypothesis-wide outcome shift.
statements.justification: The benchmark calculation kills the simplest marked-prior route before any global frontier formula is asserted.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq3\), \(h\in\{-1,1\}\), and \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\).  Elementary differentiation shows that \(x\mapsto\log(ex)/\sqrt{x}\) decreases for \(x\geq3\), so
\[
 0<\sigma_n^\star\leq\frac{\log(3e)}{\sqrt3}<\frac43.
\]
Also \(\ell_n^\star>1\).  Therefore every effect in \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}marked\text{-}family}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{|\tau_k|}{M}
 \leq\frac{\Delta_n^\star}{M}+\frac{\sigma_n^\star}{2}
 =\frac{\sigma_n^\star}{4\ell_n^\star}+\frac{\sigma_n^\star}{2}
 <1. \tag{13}
\]
Thus all displayed Bernoulli probabilities are in \([0,1]\).  Their conditional means are
\[
 E[Y(a)\mid X=k]
 =\frac M2\left[2\left\{\frac12+\frac{(2a-1)\tau_k}{2M}\right\}-1\right]
 =\frac{(2a-1)\tau_k}{2}=\mu_{ak},
\]
which obey the mean envelope by (13), and their conditional central variances are at most \(M^2/4\), hence obey the second-moment envelope.  The construction draws \(A\) independently of both potential outcomes conditional on \(X\) and sets \(Y=Y(A)\); consequently conditional exchangeability and consistency hold.  Its propensity is \(1/2\), which obeys overlap because \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

Exact mass normalization follows from \(p_k=1/n\) for \(1\leq k\leq n\).  Since \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) has \(\sum_kz_k=0\),
\[
 \tau(P_{h,z}^\star)
 =\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\left(h\Delta_n^\star+\frac{M\sigma_n^\star}{2}z_k\right)
 =h\Delta_n^\star, \tag{14}
\]
and, for every occupied cell,
\[
 |\tau_k-\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)|
 =\frac{M\sigma_n^\star}{2}|z_k|
 \leq\frac{M\sigma_n^\star}{2}
 \leq M\sigma_n^\star. \tag{15}
\]
Equations (13)--(15) and the preceding checks prove \(P_{h,z}^\star\in\mathcal P_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}\).  They also prove that both mixture hypotheses have the identical deterministic design \((p_k,\pi_k)=(1/n,1/2)\), and that their ATE supports are the singletons \(\{h\Delta_n^\star\}\).

For the distance calculation set \(Z_i=(2A_i-1)Y_i\).  Conditional on any fixed \((h,z)\), the \(Z_i\) are iid, lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\), and satisfy
\[
 E[Z_i\mid h,z]
 =\sum_{k=1}^n\frac1n\sum_{a=0}^1\frac12(2a-1)\mu_{ak}
 =\frac12\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)
 =\frac{h\Delta_n^\star}{2}. \tag{16}
\]
For completeness, let a random variable \(V\) lie in \([a,b]\), put \(p=(EV-a)/(b-a)\), and set \(t=\lambda(b-a)\).  Convexity of the exponential gives
\[
 E e^{\lambda(V-EV)}
 \leq e^{-pt}\{1-p+pe^t\}.
\]
If \(g(t)=\log[e^{-pt}\{1-p+pe^t\}]\), then \(g(0)=g'(0)=0\), while \(g''(t)\) is the variance of a Bernoulli variable under an exponential tilt and hence is at most \(1/4\).  Integrating this inequality twice, for either sign of \(t\), gives \(g(t)\leq t^2/8\).  With \(b-a=M\),
\[
 E\exp\{\lambda(V-EV)\}\leq\exp(\lambda^2M^2/8). \tag{17}
\]
Exponential Markov inequality applied to (16), optimized at \(\lambda=2\Delta_n^\star/M^2\), therefore yields uniformly in \(z\)
\[
 Q_{P_{1,z}^\star}^{(n)}(\overline Z_n\leq0)
 \leq\exp\left\{-\frac{n(\Delta_n^\star)^2}{2M^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 Q_{P_{-1,z}^\star}^{(n)}(\overline Z_n\geq0)
 \leq\exp\left\{-\frac{n(\Delta_n^\star)^2}{2M^2}\right\}. \tag{18}
\]
Integrating (18) over the two uniform priors preserves both bounds.  With \(B=\{\overline Z_n>0\}\), the variational definition of total variation then gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_{-1}^\star,\mathbb Q_1^\star)
 &\geq \mathbb Q_1^\star(B)-\mathbb Q_{-1}^\star(B)\\
 &\geq1-2\exp\left\{-\frac{n(\Delta_n^\star)^2}{2M^2}\right\}\\
 &=1-2\exp\left\{-\frac{\log^2(en)}{32\log^2(e+\log^2(en))}\right\},
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality uses the definitions of \(\sigma_n^\star\), \(\ell_n^\star\), and \(\Delta_n^\star\).  The exponent tends to infinity because \(\log(en)/\log(e+\log^2(en))\to\infty\).  Hence the lower bound on total variation tends to one and in particular exceeds \(1/3\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The full-mixture indistinguishability condition fails despite exact normalization, common design, and realization-wise radius control; equation (16) identifies the hypothesis-wide outcome shift as the cause.

statements.statement: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), carry out \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}repair\text{-}handle}\): determine the maximal \(\rho_n\) for supportwise feasible, exactly normalized priors with identical design marginals, ATEs concentrated in disjoint intervals separated by \(M\rho_n\), and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\). Prove either \(\rho_n\sqrt n\to\infty\), which supplies a substantive same-class lower bound inside the accepted parent's residual wedge, or a quantitative obstruction showing that this conditionally centered shared-design program cannot exceed the parametric separation order. Only a benchmark construction that passes exact normalization, realization-wise radius, target concentration, and full-mixture distance may be extended across \(\mathcal W\); no global rate formula is committed before that test.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine whether a supportwise radius-valid, exactly normalized, conditionally centered shared-design marked coupling at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\) can attain \(\rho_n\sqrt n\to\infty\), or prove that every coupling in a precisely specified version of that program has \(\rho_n=O_{\epsilon}(n^{-1/2})\).
obligation.obstruction: The construction handle does not define the mark-score class, the latent shared-design law, the admissible hypothesis-dependent couplings, or the conditional likelihood constraints.  Consequently its advertised maximum is not yet a well-defined optimization.  Even under the broader well-defined outer feasibility conditions, the established minimax upper bound yields only a logarithmic upper gap and does not decide the requested dichotomy.
obligation.attempted: The exactly normalized balanced-mark global-shift family was tested and fails because its first-order signed-outcome shift drives total variation to one.  A testing reduction from the refined minimax upper bound gives the outer logarithmic upper bound, while an explicit homogeneous singleton-prior pair attains parametric separation and total variation at most one third.  Neither argument controls all latent, conditionally centered shared-design couplings.
obligation.partial_result:
Define \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{outer}}\) as the supremum of the normalized distances between the two target-support intervals over all pairs of priors satisfying only exact normalization, supportwise membership in \(\mathcal P_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}\), identical design marginals, and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\), without imposing a particular centered-score representation.  The frozen results imply the rigorous outer bracket
\[
 c n^{-1/2}\le \rho_n^{\mathrm{outer}}
 \le C_{\epsilon}\log(en)n^{-1/2}.                                   \tag{6}
\]
Here is the derivation.  At \(d=n\) one has \(v_{n,n}=1\), \(u_{n,n}=\log^{-2}(en)\), and \((\sigma_n^\star)^2=\log^2(en)/n\).  The third branch of \(q_{n,n,\sigma_n^\star}^{\mathrm{em}}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:refined\text{-}bracket}\) therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathsf R_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}
 &\le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac1n+
 (\sigma_n^\star)^2\right\}\\
 &\le 3C_{\epsilon}M^2(\sigma_n^\star)^2.                            \tag{7}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last step uses \(\log(en)>1\).

Consider any feasible pair of priors whose target-support intervals \(I_{-}\) and \(I_{+}\) have distance at least \(M\rho\), and let their sample-mixture laws be \(\mathbb Q_{-}\) and \(\mathbb Q_{+}\).  Given any estimator \(T\), classify its value according to the nearer of \(I_{-}\) and \(I_{+}\), breaking ties deterministically.  If this classifier errs under hypothesis \(h\), then
\[
 |T-\tau(P)|\ge \operatorname{dist}(T,I_h)\ge \frac{M\rho}{2}.         \tag{8}
\]
Writing \(e_h\) for its error probability under \(\mathbb Q_h\), averaging (8) over the two priors yields
\[
 \frac12\sum_{h\in\{-1,1\}}\int
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P))^2],d\Pi_h(P)
 \ge \frac{M^2\rho^2}{8}(e_{-}+e_{+}).                               \tag{9}
\]
The elementary testing identity \(e_{-}+e_{+}\ge1-\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_{-},\mathbb Q_{+})\), obtained by writing the acceptance region of the classifier in the variational definition of total variation, and feasibility give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P))^2]
 \ge \frac{M^2\rho^2}{12}.                                           \tag{10}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(T\), comparing (10) with (7), and taking square roots proves
\[
 \rho\le 6\sqrt{C_{\epsilon}}\,\sigma_n^\star
 =6\sqrt{C_{\epsilon}}\,\frac{\log(en)}{\sqrt n}.                  \tag{11}
\]

For the lower side of (6), fix \(0<c\le1/3\).  Under hypothesis \(h\in\{-1,1\}\), use the singleton prior on the law with \(p_k=1/n\), \(\pi_k=1/2\), and \(\tau_k=hcM/\sqrt n\) for every \(k\).  Set \(\mu_{ak}=(2a-1)\tau_k/2\).  Conditional on \(X=k\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), draw potential outcomes independently of \(A\) with
\[
 P\{Y(a)=M/2\mid X=k\}
 =\frac12+\frac{(2a-1)\tau_k}{2M},                                   \tag{12}
\]
and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  Since \(|\tau_k|=cM/\sqrt n\le M\), (12) is a probability.  It gives
\[
 E[Y(a)\mid X=k]=\frac{(2a-1)\tau_k}{2}=\mu_{ak},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Y(a)\mid X=k)
 =\frac{M^2}{4}-\mu_{ak}^2\le M^2.                                  \tag{13}
\]
Thus consistency follows from \(Y=Y(A)\), exchangeability follows because \(A\) is drawn independently of the potential outcomes conditionally on \(X\), overlap holds because \(\pi_k=1/2\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), the mean and variance envelopes follow from (13), and the radius is zero because every \(\tau_k\) equals \(\tau(P)=hcM/\sqrt n\).  Hence both laws belong to the frozen class.  Their ATE singleton supports are separated by \(2cM/\sqrt n\).

Put \(t=c/(2\sqrt n)\).  Conditional on either value of \((X,A)\), the two hypotheses induce Bernoulli probabilities \(1/2+t\) and \(1/2-t\) on the sign of \(Y\), in one order or the other.  Their Hellinger affinity is
\[
 2\sqrt{(1/2+t)(1/2-t)}=\sqrt{1-4t^2}.                                \tag{14}
\]
The design law is identical, so (14) is also the one-observation affinity.  Independence makes the \(n\)-observation affinity
\[
 \mathcal A_n=(1-4t^2)^{n/2}.                                         \tag{15}
\]
For dominated laws with densities \(p,q\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\) gives \(\operatorname{TV}(p,q)\le\sqrt{1-(\int\sqrt{pq})^2}\).  Using (15) and Bernoulli's inequality, which applies because \(0\le4t^2\le1\), yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_{-},\mathbb Q_{+})
 \le\sqrt{1-(1-4t^2)^n}
 \le2\sqrt n\,t=c\le\frac13.                                      \tag{16}
\]
This feasible pair has \(\rho=2c/sqrt n\), proving the lower side of (6).  The pair is a small global shift and does not instantiate the undefined conditionally centered marked-score mechanism.  Thus (6) neither produces a super-parametric feasible centered coupling nor proves a parametric obstruction for every such coupling.

statements.justification: This isolates the first converse calculation after removing both the empirical region and the already-closed \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\) approximation region.
statements.gap: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), neither closed-region condition holds.  The outer separation bracket remains logarithmically nonmatching, and the conditionally centered marked-score program is not specified tightly enough to decide whether super-parametric separation is feasible.
statements.consumer: A benchmark construction passing normalization, realization-wise radius, target concentration, and full-mixture distance would justify extending a rare-cell converse into the corrected residual wedge; a universal parametric obstruction would rule out that architecture.

statements.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}moment\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:maximal\text{-}effect\text{-}radius}\), the clipped matched-cell occupancy estimator \(\widetilde\tau\) computed from the first \(m_0\) observations satisfies, for \(n\geq 8\),
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(P))^2\right]
 \leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\sigma^2+\frac1{m_0}+\frac d{m_0^2}\right)
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  The statement is the rescaled real-outcome, bounded-conditional-second-moment form of the published matched-cell occupancy bound.

source.verbatim_statement: The bias and variance of \widehat{\tau} are bounded as |\mathbb{E}[\widehat{\tau}-\psi]|\leq\sigma_n+2\exp(-C(\epsilon)n^2/(n\vee d)) and \operatorname{Var}(\widehat{\tau})\lesssim\sigma_n^2+d/n^2+1/n, where C(\epsilon) and the implicit constant depend on \epsilon. The binary nature of Y is assumed primarily for simplicity and is not essential; the rates remain valid when \mathbb{E}[Y^2\mid X=k,A=a]\leq C, which holds with bounded conditional variance.
